source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    check option can be enable/disable

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/AccountService 2>&1 | jq "{MinimumPasswordLength, AccountLockoutThreshold, AccountLockoutDuration, AccountLockoutCounterResetAfter}" 2>/dev/null; echo ---ipmi---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" user list 2>&1 | head
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL Redfish AccountService policy JSON + IPMI user list so the user confirms the password/lockout policy settings; modifying policy is a write the user drives.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: reading policies is read-only; changing lockout/password policy is a state change, user-driven.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL correctly separates reads from security writes, but assumes Policies means four AccountService password/lockout fields even though the source never identifies the option. The command bypasses TLS, exposes credentials, truncates unrelated user data and performs no enable/disable or enforcement checkpoint.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires a Project-defined policy matrix, complete field coverage, temporary-account enforcement, independent recovery and restore. V3.1 further refuses to collapse unknown WebUI toggles into numeric AccountService fields until the actual firmware page/control inventory is captured.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 922/2291 accepts the assumed fields conditionally but does not resolve which option is toggled, whether the properties are writable/boolean, how UI/API agree, how enforcement is observed or how access is recovered.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: User management owns account lifecycle; Sessions owns active sessions. Password/lockout, session timeout, protocol enablement or other WebUI policies must be explicitly named rather than inferred from adjacent rows.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1084, Wistron-BMC-00213-V002 or 84d8bc0ad97d000f draft exists in the invalidated run.
historical_reviews.v3: No V3 overlay exists for this exact case.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves the generic `option` wording; ED-34 treats control identity/allowed values as Project readiness inputs; ED-35 retains actual enable/disable enforcement rather than read-only display; ED-38 requires per-control approval, recovery, restoration and no automatic retry.

original_test_intent: Verify each Project-approved BMC security-policy option in scope can be enabled and disabled through its original WebUI control, persists with the documented API value and actually enforces the expected behavior without weakening or losing recovery access.
original_method: First inventory the exact Policies page/control labels, types, current values, supported ranges and backing resources for the selected firmware; choose one explicitly approved low-risk control and test value at a time; capture baseline, save the change through WebUI, read back UI/API, exercise a bounded temporary-account enforcement check, restore the original value and verify independent administration before continuing.
manual_activity: An engineer names the actual in-scope options, approves enable/disable values and safe enforcement probes, and protects recovery accounts. A human confirms each WebUI save. Automation can inventory backing properties and test a temporary account, but cannot infer the policy list, weaken production security or issue the verdict.
required_inputs: BMC/firmware/WebUI/Redfish identity and exact Policies page/control inventory
Per-control label, backing property, type, writable state, allowed values/ranges, dependencies and restart/session effects
Approved original/test/restore values and expected observable enforcement behavior
Temporary account and harmless bounded authentication/authorization probe
Protected current/admin/recovery accounts and independent recovery session
Secure interface credentials, audit expectations and secret-redaction plan
Per-control approval, rollback and final complete-policy comparison
safety_requirements: Do not clear BMC/security/audit logs or expose credentials, tokens, password material or unnecessary account metadata.
Do not assume generic Policies equals AccountService password/lockout fields; discover and record the actual UI control before any write.
Do not use insecure TLS, command-line passwords, truncated `user list` or a UI checkbox alone as formal policy evidence.
Never weaken production policy, lock the only administrator or test enforcement against a protected/recovery account; use a temporary account and bounded attempts.
Obtain separate approval for each control/value, change only one at a time and verify UI/API persistence plus actual enforcement before restoration.
Stop on access impact, unknown dependency, UI/API mismatch or failed restore; preserve evidence and use independent recovery without retrying another policy.
agent_execution_scope: Discover and record exact policy controls/resources, validate their semantics, approved values, temporary-account probe, protected access, audit and restoration.
Collect complete redacted baseline across WebUI/API and current recovery/session state; present one selected control for point-of-action confirmation.
After human WebUI save, read back the actual property, execute only the approved bounded enforcement probe, collect audit evidence and restore/reverify baseline.
Stop without guessed fields, insecure transport, production weakening, bulk writes, automatic next-control/retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Define the in-scope WebUI policy options and authoritative enable/disable semantics for this firmware.
Approve one-at-a-time test/restore values, temporary-account enforcement probes, access safeguards and recovery.
Review per-control UI/API/persistence/enforcement/audit/restore evidence and issue formal verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: At best a partial discovery hint. The chosen numeric fields may not be the source's toggle, `user list` is not policy enforcement, output is truncated and credentials/TLS are unsafe. No enable/disable, persistence, enforcement or restore occurs.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Discover the actual vendor WebUI policy control and backing resource first. Then use the source WebUI for one approved toggle/value and protected API readback, with a bounded temporary-account enforcement check and exact restore.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The generic Policies identity, enable/disable wording, no Script, DeepSeek AccountService/ipmitool proposal/risk and 5/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review does not invent a specific option or treat zero machine time as read-only scope.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a firmware-specific policy-control matrix, then test each approved option as an isolated WebUI save/readback/enforcement/restore checkpoint using a temporary account and independent recovery.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC firmware's actual Security and access Policies page and backing service.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC/WebUI/Redfish/IPMI versions, authentication provider, policy schema and audit revision.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor policy/control/enforcement specification, Project RBAC/password/session security baseline and recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Turns an unnamed toggle into an authoritative control matrix with persistence, enforcement, audit and recovery while preserving the original functional enable/disable requirement.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Readback does not prove enforcement; API writes may not prove WebUI control; numeric password values are not generic booleans; one policy cannot stand in for all in-scope controls.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Control identity/semantics, values, enforcement probe, protected access, audit and restoration.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong policy change can weaken authentication or lock out management; some controls affect only new sessions or require service restart.

project_override_considerations: A Project may select only the policy controls applicable to its SPEC and may use an approved API/vendor tool, but must record original WebUI coverage, actual control/value, reason, engineer approval, enforcement equivalence and any uncovered UI behavior. Read-only inspection is partial evidence, not enable/disable completion.
expected_evidence: Target/version identity, authoritative in-scope policy-control matrix with UI label/resource/type/allowed values/dependencies and protected recovery baseline
Complete redacted pre-change WebUI/API values, temporary-account state, active sessions and audit baseline
Per-control approval, WebUI save/audit, exact persisted API value and any required service/session transition
Bounded temporary-account enforcement result showing expected enabled versus disabled behavior without protected-access impact
Exact restore and final complete-policy/session comparison, no secret exposure/bulk/retry, coverage limits and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently request enable/disable behavior for Policies. The policy option is unnamed and materially under-specified, but Project/vendor discovery can identify it; there are no competing targets or operations in the source.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The policy-toggle purpose is identifiable. A firmware-specific control inventory and Project matrix can define the exact option and safe enforcement, so missing inputs make execution pending rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps PACKAGE but rejects the assumed/truncated read-only AccountService shortcut and requires actual named WebUI control, enforcement and restore.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on critical hybrid controls and strengthens source-specific control discovery before accepting its password/lockout examples.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces generic command sanity with a one-control state machine and protected enforcement evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps account lifecycle and session disconnect separate while using only defined temporary-account effects for policy enforcement.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents arbitrary AccountService fields or a user list from being reported as the unnamed policy's enable/disable result and prevents a broad security change from locking out recovery access.
independent_technical_reasoning: A policy exists to change enforcement, so neither UI state nor API value alone is enough. Because the source does not name the control, the first engineering step is a firmware-specific inventory, not a guessed mapping. Once selected, each control must be isolated through baseline, one write, bounded behavior, restore and independent access verification to distinguish persistence from effective policy and to contain security blast radius.
